title: Euclid telescope spots oldest quasars ever discovered, adding to "perplexing" space mystery
facts: An international team of astronomers discovered 31 ancient quasars using the European Space Agency's Euclid telescope.
The Euclid space telescope operates at a stable hovering spot approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
The newly discovered group of 31 ancient quasars includes the two oldest quasars observed to date.
The light from the two oldest discovered quasars originated when the universe was roughly 670 million years old.
The universe is currently estimated to be 13.8 billion years old.
The recent Euclid telescope discovery beats the previous 2021 record for the oldest known quasar by around 20 million years.
The European Space Agency launched the Euclid space telescope in 2023.
The Euclid telescope has doubled the number of ancient quasars known to science within just two years of operation.
Daming Yang is the lead author of the quasar study published in Astronomy & Astrophysics.
The newly discovered quasars date back to a period of the early universe known as the epoch of reionization.
The James Webb space telescope has also recently observed the newly announced ancient quasars.
The Euclid mission aims to chart one-third of the sky to study dark matter and dark energy.
The Euclid telescope captured an image packed with 60 million stars at the center of the Milky Way galaxy.
The Euclid telescope captured an image in 2024 of the Abell 2390 galaxy cluster containing more than 50,000 galaxies.
The Abell 2390 galaxy cluster is located 2.7 billion light years away from Earth.
